LESSON: PEACEFUL COEXISTENCE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People, Population and Relationships
Topic 2.6: Peaceful Coexistence
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Peaceful Coexistence, part of People, Population and Relationships in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How do varied personalities shape society? 2. Why is respect and appreciation of diversity crucial for social cohesion?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Peaceful Coexistence together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Respect: Learners display humility as they listen to each other as they brainstorm personality attributes which make

individuals different from others.

• Unity: Learners collaborate with others as they role play in class the unique personality attributes to enhance self- awareness.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Self-esteem: Learners compose and recite poems which propagate a culture of respect among learners and present.

● Self-awareness: Learners role play in class the unique personality attributes to enhance self-awareness.

● Decision Making: Learners categorise personality attributes into desirable and undesirable

Link to other Learning Areas:

● English, Kiswahili and Kenyan Sign Language: Learners brainstorm on personal attributes which make them

different from others.

● Creative Arts: Learners compose and recite poems which propagate respect and appreciation of diversity.
